The '''1978 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 92nd staging of the All-Ireland [[hurling]] championship since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The championship began on 30 April 1978 and ended on 3 September 1978.

[[Cork GAA|Cork]] entered the championship as [[1977 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-06-06 |title=Flashback: Nine of the best action shots from All-Ireland hurling final clashes in the 1970s |url=https://www.independent.ie/archives/flashback-nine-of-the-best-action-shots-from-all-ireland-hurling-final-clashes-in-the-1970s/34775885.html |access-date=2024-12-04 |website=Irish Independent |language=en}}</ref>

On 3 September 1978, Cork won the championship following a 1–15 to 2–8 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=108922|title=Cork's three-in-a-row 70s hurling teams honoured|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=23 March 2009|access-date=31 October 2013}}</ref> This was their 24th All-Ireland title, their third championship in succession.

Kilkenny's [[Liam O'Brien (hurler)|Liam "Chunky" O'Brien]] was the championship's top scorer with 1–23. Cork's [[John Horgan (hurler)|John Horgan]] was the choice for Hurler of the Year.

==Championship statistics==

===Miscellaneous===

* Cork retain the All-Ireland title for a third successive season. It is the fourth time in their history that they have achieved this feat and the first time since Cork in 1954 that a team has won three championships in succession.
* Kerry return to the Munster Senior Hurling Championship for the first time since 1958.
